q: The electric potentials of charged conductors are expressed relative to the electric potential of the ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potentials of charged conductors are expressed relative to the electric potential of the earth.

q: The earth is a ____ of enormous size.
e: The earth is a conductor of enormous size. Conductor is what this statement is using.

q: When compared to the size of the earth the number of electrons gained or lost by it is very small so that the ____ of the earth does not change.
e: When compared to the size of the earth the number of electrons gained or lost by it is very small so that the net charge of the earth does not change. Net charge is what this statement is using.

q: The electric potential of a conductor becomes ____ when it is connected to the earth.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential of a conductor becomes zero when it is connected to the earth.

q: Suppose a positively charged body is connected to the earth as shown in Figure 9.11(a), electrons flow ____.
c: from the earth to the body
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Suppose a positively charged body is connected to the earth as shown in Figure 9.11(a), electrons flow from the earth to the body.

q: In both cases, the electron flow takes place until the sphere has ____.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. In both cases, the electron flow takes place until the sphere has no net charge.
